title: ATLAS graph neural network enables first observation of four-top-quark production
summary: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance. The measured cross-section is 22.5⁺⁶·⁶₋₅·₅ fb, consistent with the Standard Model prediction within 1.8σ. A graph neural network separated the four-top signal from dominant backgrounds in the signal extraction.
ai_technology: Event-level graph neural network built with graph_nets/TensorFlow

evidence.tested: Using 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton–proton collisions, ATLAS observed simultaneous production of four top quarks in same-sign dilepton and multilepton events, with 6.1σ observed (4.3σ expected) significance.
evidence.unknown: This is an ATLAS observation from its own 140 fb⁻¹ analysis after earlier ATLAS/CMS evidence; it is one paper-level observation, not a separate count for CMS or later combinations. The measured cross-section uncertainty is large and its central value is 1.8σ above the SM prediction, so this is not evidence of a significant deviation from the Standard Model. Background control regions and systematic uncertainties are part of the analysis.
evidence.ai_role: The GNN discriminant classified events using a fully connected graph of reconstructed jets, leptons and missing transverse momentum, with node, edge and global features. It separated four-top signal from background and supplied the discriminant used in the signal extraction and cross-section fit.
